title: Preparing for and responding to hazards

match.reason: The new point covers the whole cycle of forecasting, warnings, building rules, levees and fire plans before a hazard, then response and recovery after it, for all hazards. The closest bank points cover only part of this: one is limited to geomorphological hazards with no response or recovery, and the other is a prevention, mitigation and preparedness classification with no response or recovery.

draft.title: Preparing for and responding to hazards
card: Communities can reduce harm before a hazard strikes. They use forecasting and warnings to give people time to act.
They can also set building rules, build levees (raised banks that hold back water) and make fire plans, so homes and people are better protected.
After a hazard, emergency services carry out the response: rescue, shelter, food and medical care.
Recovery comes later. It means repairing homes, roads and services and helping people rebuild their lives.
draft.remember: Prepare before with forecasts, warnings, rules and plans. Respond and recover after.

a.q: Which action is preparation before a hazard, rather than a response after it?
opts: Issuing a warning when a storm is forecast
Rescuing people from a flooded street
Setting up an evacuation centre for families
Rebuilding a road that was washed away
a.why: A warning is given before the hazard arrives, so people have time to act. Rescuing, sheltering and rebuilding all happen after the hazard has struck. Setting up a centre is the tempting one, but it is part of the emergency response.
a.clue: Which action happens before the hazard arrives?

b.q: A council in a river town builds a levee and changes its building rules so new houses sit higher. What are these actions?
opts: Preparation that reduces harm before a hazard
Emergency response that rescues people during a hazard
Recovery that rebuilds the town after a hazard
Forecasting that predicts when a hazard will happen
b.why: A levee and new building rules are put in place before a hazard, to reduce the harm it can cause. They are not rescue or rebuilding, which come after. Forecasting is tempting, but it predicts a hazard and does not change the town's buildings.
b.clue: Were these actions done before or after the hazard?

a.best: Issuing a warning when a storm is forecast

b.best: Preparation that reduces harm before a hazard

problems.detail: The option 'Setting up an evacuation centre for families' is ambiguous. In Australia, evacuation centres are often opened before a cyclone or bushfire arrives, so a student could reasonably see it as action taken before the hazard. A wrong option that clearly happens after impact would be safer, such as handing out food parcels after a flood.
